test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1): Morning Practice - Day 1
subject: general
question: ​What was the primary purpose of the Mansabdari system under Akbar?

options.text: To establish control over the southern kingdoms.
To organize the military and nobility for efficient administration.
To encourage the formation of private armies.
To facilitate foreign trade and commerce.

solution:
The correct answer is __**To organize the military and nobility for efficient administration.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Mansabdari system** was introduced by **Akbar** in the Mughal Empire to establish a centralized and efficient administrative structure for both military and civil governance.
 
• The term **"Mansab"** refers to "rank" or "position," and it determined the status, salary, and number of troops a Mansabdar (rank-holder) was required to maintain for the empire.
 
• The system categorized Mansabdars into grades, ranging from **10 to 10,000**, based on their rank, with higher ranks commanding larger numbers of troops and receiving higher salaries.
 
• The primary purpose of the Mansabdari system was to create a structured and organized military force that was directly controlled by the emperor, ensuring loyalty and reducing the power of regional governors and nobles.
 
• The Mansabdari system also served as an administrative tool to manage the vast Mughal Empire, as Mansabdars were often assigned both military and civil responsibilities in their designated territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ranking System:**

 
 
• The Mansabdari system was divided into two ranks - **Zat** and **Sawar**.
 
• The **Zat rank** determined the individual's personal status and salary.
 
• The **Sawar rank** indicated the number of cavalrymen a Mansabdar was required to maintain and provide during wartime.
 
 
 
• **Recruitment and Payment:**
 
 
• Mansabdars were primarily recruited based on merit, loyalty, and lineage.
 
• Their salaries were often paid through the assignment of **Jagirs (land revenue)**, though the revenue was collected by the state and then distributed to the Mansabdars.
 
 
 
• **Administrative Importance:**
 
 
• The Mansabdari system ensured that the Mughal emperor had a **well-disciplined and efficient military force**.
 
• It also centralized power in the hands of the emperor, reducing the autonomy of provincial rulers.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the System:**
 
 
• Over time, the Mansabdari system became corrupt, with Mansabdars often misreporting troop numbers or embezzling funds.
 
• The inability to maintain the system efficiently was one of the factors contributing to the decline of the Mughal Empire.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Mansabdari system was inspired by the **Persian administrative and military practices** and adapted to suit the needs of the Mughal Empire.
 
• It played a crucial role in consolidating Akbar’s rule over a vast and diverse empire.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Systems:**
 
 
• The Mansabdari system was unique compared to earlier systems like the **Iqtadari system** used during the Delhi Sultanate, as it combined both military and civil administration under centralized control.
 
• It also differed from the feudal systems in Europe, as Mansabdars were not hereditary lords but appointed officials under the emperor's command.
